examples.ko: 율동적인 음악에 맞춰 아이들이 춤을 췄어요.
examples.en: The children danced to the rhythmic music.
The waves rolled in and out rhythmically.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 선이 율동적이라서 살아 움직이는 것 같아요.
examples.en: The lines in this painting are so rhythmic that it seems alive.
He is a person whose rhythmic stride stands out.

examples.ko: 시의 율동적인 느낌을 소리 내어 읽으며 느껴 봤어요.
examples.en: I felt the rhythmic quality of the poem by reading it aloud.

examples.ko: 율동적인 동작을 따라 하니까 운동이 돼요.
examples.en: Following the rhythmic movements works as exercise.

explain: '율동'은 유치원에서 노래에 맞춰 하는 춤 동작을 가리킬 때도 많이 써요. '율동적'은 말투가 조금 딱딱해서 일상에서는 '리듬감 있는'이라고 하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 리듬감 있는 노래라서 저절로 몸이 움직여요.
phrases.en: It's a rhythmic song, so my body moves on its own.
phrases.nuance_ko: '율동적인'보다 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual, everyday way to say 'rhythmic' than 율동적인.

phrases.en: The movements of this dance are rhythmic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장 끝에서 서술어로 쓸 때는 '이다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 이다 when you use it as the predicate at the end of a sentence.

phrases.en: The dancer's rhythmic movements were beautiful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 춤이나 몸짓처럼 움직임을 꾸밀 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for describing movement such as dance or gestures.

explain_en: '율동' is also widely used for the simple dance moves kids do to songs at kindergarten. '율동적' sounds a bit stiff, so in everyday speech people often say '리듬감 있는' instead.

examples.ko: 주말에 미술 전람회를 보러 갈 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to see an art exhibition this weekend.
The exhibition runs for a week starting today.
The school held an exhibition of students' works.
I found a painting I liked at the exhibition.
There is no admission fee for that exhibition.

examples.ko: 친구와 함께 전람회장에 갔더니 사람이 정말 많았어요.
examples.en: I went to the exhibition hall with a friend and it was really crowded.

explain: '전시회'와 비슷하지만 전람회는 조금 격식 있게 들리고, 일상 대화에서는 '전시회'를 더 자주 써요. 상품과 산업을 크게 보여 주는 행사는 '박람회'라고 해요. 발음은 [절람회]예요.

phrases.en: Do you want to go to an exhibition together this weekend?
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 '전시회'가 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but 전시회 is more common in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: The school is holding an exhibition next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 준비해서 보여 줄 때 '열다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 열다 when organizing and holding an exhibition.

phrases.en: I saw many beautiful paintings at the exhibition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 나타내는 '에서'가 붙은 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the place with the particle 에서.

explain_en: It is similar to '전시회', but 전람회 sounds a bit more formal, and '전시회' is more common in everyday talk. A large event showing products and industries is called '박람회'. It is pronounced [절람회].

t90.ax: I found a painting I liked at the exhibition.

examples.en: The athlete aims at the target.
I aimed the water gun at my friend.

examples.ko: 먼저 조준하고 숨을 멈춘 뒤에 쏘세요.
examples.en: Aim first, hold your breath, and then shoot.
I aimed slowly and shot the arrow.
When aiming, I close one eye.
The gaze aiming at the target is sharp.

explain: '과녁을 조준하다'처럼 대상을 '을/를'로 받아요. 일상에서는 '겨냥하다'도 자주 쓰고, 비유로 '시장을 겨냥하다'라고 하면 '조준하다'보다 더 자연스러워요. 총, 활, 물총을 쏘기 직전의 동작이에요.

phrases.en: My friend aimed at me and sprayed water.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조준하다'와 뜻이 가깝고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to 조준하다 and more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: You have to aim exactly to hit it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정확히'를 붙여 맞히기 위한 조건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '정확히' states the condition for hitting the target.

phrases.en: The player is aiming at the target now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 있다'로 지금 하는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-고 있다' describes the action in progress.

explain_en: Literally aiming a weapon or bow at a target. It takes its target with the object particle, as in '과녁을 조준하다'. In daily speech '겨냥하다' is also common, and figuratively '시장을 겨냥하다' sounds more natural than 조준하다. It is the action right before shooting a gun, bow, or water gun.

t90.ax: When aiming, I close one eye.

examples.en: I sang songs with my friends in front of the campfire.
We had a campfire on the last day of the retreat.
The light of the campfire was really warm.
The campfire was canceled because of rain.
We sat around the campfire and roasted marshmallows.
The kids are looking forward to the campfire the most.

explain: 캠핑이나 수련회에서 모여 앉아 즐기는 불 행사를 말해요. 불 자체는 '모닥불'이라고 해요. '캠프파이어를 하다'처럼 행사 느낌으로 쓰고, '모닥불을 피우다'처럼 불을 지핀다는 느낌으로도 써요.

phrases.en: We had a campfire by the lake at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사나 모임으로서 즐긴다는 느낌으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has the feel of enjoying it as an event or gathering.

phrases.en: We sat around the bonfire and talked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사보다는 불 자체를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the fire itself rather than the event.

phrases.en: We roasted marshmallows at the campfire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 나타내는 조사와 함께 쓰는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with a place particle to show location.

explain_en: It refers to the event of gathering around a fire at a camp or retreat. The fire itself is '모닥불'. You say '캠프파이어를 하다' for the event and '모닥불을 피우다' for lighting the fire.

examples.en: Beaches usually close at the end of August.
What time does the amusement park close?

examples.ko: 날씨가 추워져서 올해는 일찍 폐장하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Because it got cold, they decided to close early this year.

examples.ko: 시장이 벌써 폐장했으니까 내일 다시 가요.
examples.en: The market has already closed, so let's go again tomorrow.

examples.ko: 스키장은 봄이 되면 폐장하는 곳이 많아요.
examples.en: Many ski resorts close when spring comes.
Let's have one last swim before it closes for the season.

explain: 주로 해수욕장, 스키장, 시장, 놀이공원처럼 계절이나 하루의 영업을 끝낼 때 써요. 반대말은 '개장하다'예요. 가게 문을 닫을 때는 보통 '문을 닫다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: The amusement park's closing time is 10 p.m.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하루 영업이 끝나는 시간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the time when the day's business ends.

phrases.en: The beach's closing day is near, so it's crowded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절 영업을 끝내는 날을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the day when seasonal business ends.

phrases.en: The market closes at 6 p.m.
phrases.nuance_ko: '폐장하다'보다 말할 때 훨씬 자연스러운 일상 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A much more natural everyday expression than 폐장하다.

explain_en: Beaches, pools or ski areas end the season. It is mainly used when places like beaches, ski resorts, markets and amusement parks end their season or their day. The opposite is '개장하다' (to open). For a normal shop, people usually say '문을 닫다'.

dis.h: a venue shuts for the season

p.n: The passive stresses that it is closed by schedule; the active one is just 'closes'. Both are fine.

examples.ko: 그 피아니스트는 다음 달에 오케스트라와의 협연을 앞두고 있어요.
examples.en: That pianist has a concerto performance with an orchestra coming up next month.

examples.ko: 이번 콘서트에서는 두 가수의 협연 무대가 있어요.
examples.en: This concert will have a joint stage with two singers.
We gathered from the morning to rehearse the joint performance.

examples.ko: 그 바이올리니스트는 협연 경험이 아주 많아요.
examples.en: That violinist has a lot of experience performing with orchestras.

examples.ko: 협연 덕분에 평소 듣기 어려운 조합을 즐겼어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the joint performance, I enjoyed a combination I rarely get to hear.
The joint performance by the student and teacher was really moving.

explain: 독주자가 오케스트라나 다른 연주자와 함께 무대에 서는 것을 말해요. 모두 비슷한 역할로 함께 연주하는 '합주'와는 조금 달라요.

phrases.example: 그 바이올리니스트는 내년에 유명한 오케스트라와 협연을 해요.
phrases.en: That violinist will perform with a famous orchestra next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '협연'과 '하다'를 붙여 함께 무대에 서는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combining 협연 with 하다 means to appear on stage together.

phrases.en: Today's soloist is a seventeen-year-old pianist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오케스트라와 함께 연주하는 독주자를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The soloist who plays together with an orchestra.

phrases.en: I'm looking forward to the two singers' joint performance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 서는 공연 무대를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a stage where performers appear together.

explain_en: Musicians performing together in a concert (오늘 저녁 음악회에서 두 연주자가 협연을 해요.) It refers to a soloist appearing on stage together with an orchestra or other performers. It is a little different from '합주', where everyone plays together in similar roles.

examples.ko: 큰 강물이 굽이쳐 흐르는 모습을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the big river flowing in great curves.
The waves surged and rolled, so the boat rocked a lot.
The scenery of mountain ridges winding in sweeping curves is truly magnificent.
When the wind blew, the barley field rolled like waves.
The surging current gradually became calm.
I fished in a place where the water doesn't swirl and surge.

explain: '물결치다'와 비슷하지만 굽이치다는 강이나 산줄기, 큰 파도가 길고 크게 휘어지며 움직이는 느낌이 있어요. 주로 풍경을 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 강물이 굽이쳐 흐르는 곳에 마을이 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a village where the river flows in sweeping curves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 휘어지며 흐르는 물을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for water flowing in large sweeping bends.

phrases.en: The surging waves were scary.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 '파도'를 꾸미는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describing 파도.

phrases.en: I can see the winding mountain ridge far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산이 길게 휘어 이어진 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for mountains stretching in long curves.

explain_en: It is similar to '물결치다' (to ripple), but 굽이치다 has the feel of rivers, mountain ridges or big waves moving in long, sweeping curves. It is mostly used when describing scenery.

examples.en: I sat and rested on a tree stump in the forest.

examples.ko: 나무를 베어 낸 자리에 그루터기만 남았어요.
examples.en: Only a stump was left where the tree had been cut.
A new sprout came up from the old stump.
A big stump sits there like a chair.
The kids climb up on the stump and play.

examples.ko: 그루터기의 나이테를 세어 보면 나무 나이를 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you count the rings on the stump, you can tell the tree's age.

explain: 나무나 풀을 베어 낸 뒤에 땅에 남은 부분을 말할 때 써요. 서 있는 나무의 아래쪽 줄기는 '밑동'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: When spring came, a sprout came out of the stump.
phrases.nuance_ko: 베어 낸 나무에서 새로 자라는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for new growth from a cut-down tree.
phrases.en_equiv: a sprout grows from a stump

phrases.example: 가을 논에는 벼 그루터기가 남아 있어요.
phrases.en: In the autumn rice fields, rice stubble remains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무뿐 아니라 곡식을 베고 남은 밑부분에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used not only for trees but also for the base left after harvesting grain.

phrases.en: I tripped over a stump and fell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숲길이나 산길에서 일어나는 일을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for something happening on a forest or mountain path.

explain_en: You use it for the part left in the ground after a tree or plant is cut down. The lower part of a tree that is still standing is called '밑동'.

examples.en: When spring came, the plum tree's buds burst open.

examples.ko: 꽃망울이 맺힌 걸 보니 곧 필 것 같아요.
examples.en: Seeing the buds form, they look like they'll bloom soon.

examples.ko: 아직 꽃망울만 있어서 벚꽃이 안 피었어요.
examples.en: There are only buds so far, so the cherry blossoms haven't bloomed.

examples.ko: 아침에 보니 꽃망울에 이슬이 맺혀 있어요.
examples.en: This morning I saw dew on the flower buds.
The little buds are opening one by one.

examples.ko: 장미 꽃망울은 아직 단단히 닫혀 있어요.
examples.en: The rose buds are still tightly closed.

explain: '꽃봉오리'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, 아직 피지 않았거나 막 피려는 꽃을 가리켜요. '꽃망울을 터뜨리다'는 꽃이 피기 시작한다는 말과 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: Rose buds have formed in the garden.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같은 말이라 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, so they are interchangeable.

phrases.en: Small buds have formed on every branch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 피기 전에 봉오리가 생긴 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when buds have formed but flowers haven't opened yet.

phrases.en: The cherry blossoms finally burst into bloom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 피기 시작한다는 뜻으로 봄 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means flowers begin to bloom; common in talk about spring.

explain_en: Small bud ready to burst open, poetic and spring-like. It can be used the same way as '꽃봉오리', and refers to a flower that has not opened yet or is about to. It goes well with '꽃망울을 터뜨리다', meaning a flower starts to bloom.

t90.ax: The little buds are opening one by one.

examples.en: In the old days, mules carried loads.
A mule is born from a horse and a donkey.
I saw an old man leading a mule on a country road.
A story about a mule and a farmer appears in the picture book.

examples.ko: 이 그림에는 노새 한 마리가 그려져 있어요.
examples.en: A mule is drawn in this picture.

examples.ko: 노새에 짐을 가득 싣고 길을 떠났어요.
examples.en: They loaded the mule with baggage and set off on the road.

explain: 당나귀와 헷갈리기 쉽지만 다른 동물이에요. 요즘은 직접 보기 어려워서 옛이야기나 그림, 책에서 주로 만나요.

phrases.example: 시골 마을에는 노새 한 마리가 살았어요.
phrases.en: A mule lived in the country village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물은 '마리'로 세므로 '한 마리'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Animals are counted with 마리, so it goes with 한 마리.

phrases.example: 옛날 그림에는 노새를 탄 사람이 나와요.
phrases.en: In old paintings, there is a person riding a mule.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 올라타고 가는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a person riding on one.

phrases.en: The mule pulls the cart up the hill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짐을 나르는 노새의 모습을 그릴 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common expression for picturing a mule hauling loads.

explain_en: It is easy to mix up with a donkey, but it is a different animal. Today it is hard to see in person, so you mostly meet it in old tales, pictures and books.

en: to sprout; to grow out; to grow thorns

examples.en: Sharp thorns have grown on the rose stem.

examples.ko: 아기 새 등에 날개가 돋치기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Wings have started to grow on the baby bird's back.

examples.ko: 그 말에 가시가 돋쳐 있어서 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: That remark had thorns in it, and it hurt me.
The new product is selling like hotcakes.

examples.ko: 가시 돋친 말은 하지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better not to say cutting words.

examples.ko: 그 선인장은 줄기마다 뾰족한 가시가 돋쳐 있어요.
examples.en: That cactus has pointy spines growing on every stem.

explain: 가시나 날개 같은 것이 몸에서 뾰족하게 나올 때 써요. 새싹이나 소름, 여드름이 나올 때는 보통 '돋다', '돋아나다'를 써요. 실제 대화에서는 '날개 돋친 듯', '가시 돋친'처럼 굳은 표현으로 가장 많이 만나요.

phrases.example: 새로 나온 과자가 날개 돋친 듯 팔리고 있어요.
phrases.en: The newly released snack is selling like hotcakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상품이 아주 빠르게 많이 팔릴 때 쓰는 관용 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An idiom for a product selling very quickly in large numbers.

phrases.example: 화가 났다고 가시 돋친 말을 하면 후회해요.
phrases.en: If you say cutting words out of anger, you'll regret it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대를 아프게 찌르는 듯한 비꼬는 말을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to sharp, sarcastic words that sting the other person.

explain_en: It is used when things like thorns or wings grow sharply out of a body. For sprouts, goosebumps or pimples, people usually say '돋다' or '돋아나다'. In real conversation you'll most often meet it in fixed expressions like '날개 돋친 듯' and '가시 돋친'.

t90.ax: It's better not to say cutting words.

en: to be cast; to hang down

examples.ko: 창가에 커튼 그림자가 길게 드리워져 있어요.
examples.en: The curtain's shadow stretches long by the window.

examples.ko: 해가 지면서 산 그림자가 마을에 드리워졌어요.
examples.en: As the sun set, the mountain's shadow fell over the village.
A look of tiredness hung over his face.
A cool shade was cast beneath the tree.

examples.ko: 겨울 아침, 골목에 짙은 안개가 드리워져 있었어요.
examples.en: On the winter morning, thick fog hung over the alley.
Moonlight softly fell across the lake.

explain: 그림자, 그늘, 안개, 커튼처럼 위에서 아래로 늘어지거나 넓게 깔리는 것에 써요. '그림자가 드리워지다'가 가장 자주 나오고, 나쁜 일의 조짐이라는 비유로도 써요. 하는 쪽은 '드리우다'예요.

phrases.example: 그 소식 이후 회사에 어두운 그림자가 드리워졌어요.
phrases.en: A dark shadow falls over something.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 나쁜 일이 생길 것 같은 불안한 분위기가 퍼진다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for an uneasy mood spreading, as if something bad is about to happen.

explain_en: It is used for things that hang down or spread wide, such as shadows, shade, fog and curtains. '그림자가 드리워지다' is the most common phrase, and it is also used figuratively for signs of bad things. The active verb is '드리우다'.

t90.ax: Moonlight softly fell across the lake.

examples.en: I waited for a whole hour under the scorching sun.
I walked in the blazing midday sun and now I feel dizzy.
There was no one on the playground where the sun beat down.
The farmers kept working in the fields even in the scorching sun.
I went into the shade of a tree to avoid the blazing sun.

examples.ko: 오늘은 땡볕이라 모자를 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: The sun is scorching today, so you must wear a hat.

explain: 여름에 아주 뜨겁게 내리쬐는 햇볕을 말해요. 그냥 '햇볕'이나 '뜨거운 햇볕'보다 구어에서 더 생생하고 힘든 느낌이 있어요. '땡볕 아래', '땡볕에서'처럼 그 안에서 고생하는 상황과 자주 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: My father worked all day in the scorching sun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜨거운 햇볕 속에서 고생하는 상황을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for working hard under the blazing sun.
phrases.en_equiv: to work in the scorching sun

phrases.en: I always wear a hat in the scorching midsummer sun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절을 앞에 붙여 한여름의 아주 뜨거운 햇볕을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the season gives the sense of the fierce midsummer sun.

phrases.en: We avoided the scorching sun and went into the shade of a tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜨거운 햇볕을 피해 그늘이나 실내로 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you get out of the sun into the shade or indoors.

explain_en: It describes the sun beating down fiercely in summer. Compared with plain '햇볕' (sunlight), it sounds more vivid and conveys hardship in spoken Korean. It often appears in phrases like '땡볕 아래' and '땡볕에서' describing someone struggling in it.

en: to surge; to move in waves; to roll

examples.en: When the wind blew, the barley field rippled like waves.
The lake is gently rippling.
The flags of the cheering crowd wave like a sea.
I looked at the sea, rolling with waves, for a long time.
Her long hair flowed in the wind, and it looked pretty.
The cheers of the people will surge through the square.

explain: 실제 물뿐 아니라 밀밭, 머리카락, 깃발, 사람들의 감정이 파도처럼 이어서 움직이는 모습에도 써요. 말할 때보다 글이나 묘사에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I looked at the rolling sea for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 명사를 꾸미는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-는' form modifies a noun.

phrases.en: The flag is rippling in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 움직이는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something moving in waves right now.

phrases.en: The people walked forward like waves.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-듯이'를 붙여 물결처럼 움직이는 모습을 비유해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-듯이', it compares a movement to waves.

explain_en: Fields, crowds or flags moving in wave patterns. It is used for real water but also for wheat fields, hair, flags and people's emotions moving in a wave-like way. You see it more in writing and description than in everyday speech.
